newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi stocks slightly higher in busy trade.
newsitem.headline: Saudi stocks slightly higher in busy trade.

text.p: Saudi Arabia's stock market ended the week to Thursday slightly higher in busy trade buoyed by good half-year financial results of some companies and banks, the Riyadh-based Bakheet Financial Advisors (BFA) said.
The all-share index closed less then one percent higher at 175.34 points from 174.32 points the previous week.
Of the 60 shares traded during the week, 21 rose, 27 fell and 12 were unchanged.
BFA put trading value at about 1.75 billion riyals ($467 million) down from last week's 2.17 billion.
Some 7.4 million shares changed hands in the week down from last week's nine million shares.
Saudi Arabia's electricity companies were among the top gainers in the week. SCECO-West closed 8.6 percent higher at 101 riyals from 93 riyals the previous week.
SCECO-Central ended the week 7.4 percent higher at 101 riyals from 94 riyals and SCECO-East rose 6.4 percent to 100 riayls from 94 riyals.
Riyad Bank shares were among the most active but they only gained one riyal closing at 277 riyals.
